issue.title: An empty string should be NULL

repository.name: cakephp
repository.description: CakePHP: The Rapid Development Framework for PHP - Official Repository

issue.body:
I faced this issue multiple times already. You can work around this issue but I think it should be a part of the ORM.

Table:
```
CREATE TABLE categories
(
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
    name VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
    meta_title VARCHAR(255)
);
```

ORM usage:
```
$entity = $this->Categories->newEntity($this->request->data);
$this->Categories->save($entity);
```

Current result:

| id | name | meta_title  |
| -------- |:------------:| ---------:|
| 1 | Test | |

Should be:

| id | name | meta_title  |
| -------- |:------------:| ---------:|
| 1 | Test | _NULL_ |

As I mentioned above you can work around this behavior with `Behaviors/Callbacks` but I think this should be something which is handled directly inside the ORM. Saving an empty string inside a NULLable field isn't the proper usage of `NULL`.

issue.title: Fix nullable field with default value in various db platforms.

repository.name: cakephp
repository.description: CakePHP: The Rapid Development Framework for PHP - Official Repository

issue.body:
null => true and a default value should create a nullable column with a default value not `DEFAULT NULL`.

Refs #9686

body:
I think with bool values there is a small bug left:

fixture row

``` php
'active_optional_notnull' => ['type' => 'boolean', 'null' => true, 'default' => false],
```

and test

``` php

        $data = [
            'string_optional_notnull' => '',
            'active_optional_notnull' => '',
        ];
        $entity = $this->Table->newEntity($data);

        $expected = [
            'string_optional_notnull' => '',
            'active_optional_notnull' => false,
        ];
        $this->assertSame($expected, $entity->toArray());
```

fails because it suddenly is "true" instead of "false here for the active_optional_notnull field.

Looks like because 'FALSE' is stored as string for schema()->column($key) `default` and therefore it cannot be checked with normal bool methods.

Workaround:
One could just use

``` php
'active_optional_notnull' => ['type' => 'boolean', 'null' => true, 'default' => 0],
```

Should we convert bool true/false to integer?
Is this issue with MySQL? The schema generation and reflection tests already cover boolean fields and getting `0` back as a default value for the reflected schema.
Re-closing as `''` being converted to `false` makes sense to me. Whether the `'default'` is `false` or `0`, doesn't change the results of `newEntity()`.
As it happens with local tests this seems to be SQLite related.
